newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada April consumer prices rise 1.7 pct on year.
newsitem.headline: Canada April consumer prices rise 1.7 pct on year.

text.p: Canada's unadjusted April consumer price index was unchanged from March and was up 1.7 percent on the year to 137.6, Statistics Canada said on Thursday.
CONSUMER PRICES - Pct chg April Mar
Adjusted month-on-month -0.1 +0.1
Unadjusted month-on-month +0.0 +0.2
Unadjusted year-on-year +1.7 +2.0
Unadjusted ex food and energy mth/mth +0.1 +0.4
Unadjusted ex food and energy yr/yr +1.8 +1.7
All-items Index (base 100=1986) 137.6 137.6
Three-month s/a (at annual terms) +0.6 +1.2

A Reuters survey of economists had forecast the seasonally adjusted CPI to rise 0.2 percent and the undadjusted CPI to rise 0.2 percent on the month. The survey also forecast year-over-year rises of 1.9 percent in the all-items and 1.8 percent in the core CPI.
The core CPI rise of 1.8 percent was well within the Bank of Canada's target range of one to three percent.

Statistics Canada said consumers paid less in April compared to a year earlier for mortgage loans, fresh vegetables and soft drinks. They paid more for new vehicles and vehicle insurance, university tuition, clothing, rental accommodation and meat.

April's 1.7 percent year-over-year increase was lower than the annual rates of 2.0 to 2.2 percent seen in the five previous months, StatsCan said. The agency said the slowdown in overall inflation was related to smaller movements in the transportation and food sectors.
On the month, price increases for clothing and several other commodities offset price declines for natural gas, gasoline and food, the federal agency said.
Since April last year, energy prices have moved up 1.7 percent, a small rise compared to the 12-month increases of 4.7 percent to 7.2 percent posted in the six previous months, StatsCan said.

Much of this deceleration was due to gasoline prices which showed annual increases of 5.3 percent to 10.8 percent over the past six month period but recorded a 0.2 percent decline in April, the agency said.
On the month, energy prices fell 1.6 percent.
Food prices 0.9 percent on the year but dropped 0.3 percent on the month.

Shoppers paid 1.1 percent more for clothing and 1.9 percent more for footwear in April compared to March, StatsCan said. A small part of the advance was linked to tax increases in the Atlantic provinces.
"The clothing and footwear sector, which has shown little strength in recent years, may be emerging from the doldrums," Statistics Canada said.
